# Release Notes

Use only for the GitHub release-note body. Do not use for PR preparation, CI monitoring, tagging, or Docker/post-release assets. `gh release create` and `gh release edit` may be used only by release-manager to apply a reviewed note body.

Release notes are mandatory for every release, including patches. Compose them from actual `vPREVIOUS..vNEW` commits and relevant code changes, not commit messages alone. Include meaningful user impact, notable security/dependency changes when relevant, and actual breaking/upgrade impact. Omit internal-only churn, developer tooling, AI instructions, CI/CD-only changes, and non-user-facing refactors. Do not invent details or links.

The body, including its first line, uses this exact order:

1. `# MedAssist-ng <version> brings <short user-facing theme>` with a natural, release-specific theme.
2. Two or three concise overview paragraphs explaining the release and practical user impact.
3. `### Key Takeaways` with 2-6 concise user-facing bullets.
4. Optionally, `See [announcements](<real URL>) for more details.` only when a real URL exists.
5. `# Change Log`.
6. Only relevant non-empty categories, in this order and exact visual style: `### &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;🚀 Features`, `### &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;🐞 Bug Fixes`, `### &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;🏎 Performance`, `### &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;🔒 Security`, `### &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;🛠 Improvements`, `### &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;📦 Dependencies`.
7. Group entries by domain using bold domain labels, concise user-facing wording, and a real linked short commit hash at every entry's end. Nested bullets are allowed only for multiple related entries in one domain. Never include PR references.
8. Put breaking or upgrade information in the overview/key takeaways, or add `### Upgrade Notes` under `# Change Log` only when relevant. Never label additive backward-compatible work as breaking.
9. End with `##### &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[View changes on GitHub](https://github.com/DanielVolz/medassist-ng/compare/vPREV...vNEW)`.

Emoji are allowed only in the required category headings. Do not use emoji in ordinary prose or bullets.

```markdown
# MedAssist-ng vX.Y.Z brings <short user-facing theme>

This release <overview paragraph>.

It also <practical impact paragraph>.

### Key Takeaways

- <user-facing takeaway>
- <user-facing takeaway>

# Change Log

### &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;🚀 Features

- **<domain>**: <user-facing description> ([abc1234](https://github.com/DanielVolz/medassist-ng/commit/<full-hash>))

### &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;🐞 Bug Fixes

- **<domain>**:
  - <related entry> ([def5678](https://github.com/DanielVolz/medassist-ng/commit/<full-hash>))

##### &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[View changes on GitHub](https://github.com/DanielVolz/medassist-ng/compare/vPREV...vNEW)
```

## Pre-Publication Gate

Before `gh release create` or `gh release edit`, manually compose and review the notes. Reject autogenerated GitHub notes, bare commit lists, one-line summaries, missing user-facing sections, and any body that fails one of these checks:

- First line matches `# MedAssist-ng <version> brings <theme>` and has a release-specific theme.
- There are 2-3 overview paragraphs before `### Key Takeaways`; it contains 2-6 bullets and precedes `# Change Log`.
- All categories use the exact required style, appear in prescribed order, and contain at least one entry.
- Each entry ends with a real linked short commit hash; there are no PR references or fabricated announcement links.
- The final line has the exact linked `View changes on GitHub` form.
- User impact is accurate; breaking/upgrade guidance appears only where warranted; no internal-only detail appears.
- The body does not contain `## What's New`, a top-level `### Where to Find It`, `**Full Changelog**:`, a generic `vX.Y.Z`-only heading, or an emoji ban that conflicts with required category headings.

Write reviewed notes to a temporary file, then use only the release-manager-authorized command:

```bash
gh release create vX.Y.Z --title "vX.Y.Z" --notes-file /tmp/release-notes-vX.Y.Z.md
gh release edit vX.Y.Z --title "vX.Y.Z" --notes-file /tmp/release-notes-vX.Y.Z.md
```

After create/edit, fetch the rendered release body and verify the exact ordering, final linked `View changes on GitHub` line, and absence of rejected markers. Immediately edit and reverify on failure.
